partner_context.their_ambition: French Polynesia is 118 islands scattered across an ocean the size of Europe — Tahiti and Moorea at the commercial heart, the Leeward Islands (Bora Bora, Raiatea, Tahaa, Huahine, Maupiti) as the luxury-resort crown, and the Tuamotu atolls and Marquesas beyond. The territory's ambition is to grow high-value, low-impact tourism without drowning its lagoons in diesel wake and noise.
partner_context.their_pressure: Every premium journey today is a compromise: a costly, weather-limited inter-island flight; a slow diesel ferry; or a fume-heavy resort speedboat. The Papeete↔Moorea channel already moves a city's worth of commuters on ageing ferries, and the protected biosphere lagoons of Fakarava and Maupiti are exactly where loud, oily craft are least welcome.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier turns the lagoons and protected channels into a silent, fast, zero-emission foiling network — the commuter spine on Tahiti↔Moorea, premium Leeward hops between the resort islands, and an aspirational Quanta-LR reach out to the atolls. The sea becomes the fastest and quietest way to move, not the roughest.

hero.title: Navier × French Polynesia — the islands, by foil
hero.subtitle: Papeete to Moorea in silence, Bora Bora to the Leewards over the reef — fast, quiet and zero-emission, while the ferries and diesel shuttles plow through the chop.
hero.what_we_do_together: We bring a foiling-electric water tier to French Polynesia — a commuter spine across the Tahiti–Moorea channel, premium inter-island hops across the Leeward Islands, and an aspirational long-range reach to the Tuamotu atolls. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet, captains and the French/EU certification path; the territory's port authority (Port Autonome de Papeete), resort groups and ferry operators bring the quays, the demand and the concession framework. Together we re-platform the South Pacific's most iconic lagoons as a silent waterway.

why_now: French Polynesia is pushing high-value, low-impact tourism exactly as its diesel ferry and resort-shuttle fleets age out and its marine-protected biospheres (Fakarava UNESCO, Maupiti) tighten on noise and emissions. The Papeete↔Vaiare corridor is already one of the highest-volume protected-water ferry routes in the South Pacific, and the Leeward resort islands — Bora Bora, Raiatea, Tahaa, Huahine — are minutes apart by sea but poorly linked. A foiling tier arrives as the demand is proven and the diesel alternative comes under regulatory and cost pressure.
multimodal_fit: A foiling vessel meets arrivals at Fa'a'ā (Papeete) international airport's waterfront and at Bora Bora's Motu Mute airport boat dock, linking the air gateway to resort motus and island quays. The water leg replaces the slowest, least pleasant segment — the diesel ferry queue, the long resort speedboat, the weather-grounded inter-island hop — with a fast, silent, scenic run over the reef.

differentiation.why_navier: A foiling-electric premium tier — silent, zero-wake and zero-emission, ideal for protected biosphere lagoons where diesel craft are least welcome — and software-defined for a fleet that improves over time. Backed by an at-scale operating network already rolling out in the Maldives, the closest analog to French Polynesia's atoll geography.

proof_points.claim: The commuter demand is already proven.
proof_points.evidence: The Papeete↔Vaiare (Moorea) channel is one of the highest-volume protected-water ferry corridors in the South Pacific — a city's worth of daily passengers on ageing diesel ferries.
proof_points.source: Port Autonome de Papeete / FP ferry data

proof_points.claim: The resort islands are built for the water.
proof_points.evidence: Bora Bora, Raiatea, Tahaa, Huahine and Maupiti form a tight Leeward cluster — minutes apart by sea, poorly linked today by flight or diesel boat.

proof_points.claim: Decarbonization and biosphere protection are mandated.
proof_points.evidence: Fakarava (UNESCO biosphere) and Maupiti's lagoon restrict high-wake, high-noise craft; the territory is pushing low-impact tourism.
~100 vessels / $100M phased rollout already underway in the Maldives — the closest operating analog to FP's atoll-and-lagoon geography.

objections.concern: Is the inter-island demand beyond Tahiti–Moorea real?
objections.response: The Leeward Islands carry a year-round luxury-resort base (Four Seasons, St Regis, Conrad, InterContinental) plus a steady charter and resident market — today fragmented across flights and diesel boats that a single foiling network consolidates.

objections.concern: How does it compare to the inter-island flight?
objections.response: On the dense Leeward legs, a Pioneer II hop is competitive point-to-point, far cheaper, weather-resilient in protected water, and berths at the resort quay rather than a remote airstrip — no transfer at either end.

objections.concern: Noise and wake in protected lagoons?
objections.response: Foiling is near-silent and produces minimal wake at cruise — purpose-built for Fakarava's biosphere and Maupiti's lagoon, where conventional craft face the tightest restrictions.
A clear first-of-class path under the French flag, software-defined controls, and an operating record in the US and the Maldives to build the French Polynesian certification case on.

phases.label: Phase 1 — the Tahiti–Moorea spine + the Bora Bora lagoon
phases.narrative: Launch the highest-volume run first — the Papeete↔Vaiare commuter channel — and the Bora Bora intra-lagoon resort and airport transfers, the densest premium water in the territory.
phases.rationale: Start where demand is already proven (the busiest ferry channel) and where premium resort transfers are most acute (Bora Bora's lagoon).

phases.label: Phase 2 — the full Leeward network
phases.narrative: Connect the Leeward crown — Bora Bora to Raiatea, Tahaa, Huahine and Maupiti — into one Pioneer II foiling network across the shared lagoons and channels.
phases.rationale: Consolidate the fragmented flight-and-diesel inter-island market into a single silent waterway across the resort islands.

phases.label: Phase 3 — cross-archipelago reach + the atolls (Quanta-LR)
phases.narrative: Add Quanta-LR hybrid reach — Tahiti to Bora Bora direct, Tahiti to the Tuamotu atolls (Rangiroa, Tikehau, Fakarava), and the long Marquesas trunk — de-seasonalising and de-fragmenting the longest legs. Long legs are flagged amber-dashed (roadmap) and never faked on a 70 nm boat.
phases.rationale: Extend the proven lagoon network offshore: the hybrid opens the atolls and cross-archipelago links that a 70 nm Pioneer II cannot reach.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captains, the maintenance and French/EU certification path, and the network playbook proven in the Maldives.
the_ask.partner_brings: Quay and jetty access (Port Autonome de Papeete, resort and ferry operators), the demand base, and the local operating, biosecurity and concession framework.
the_ask.next_step: A pilot MOU on the Papeete↔Moorea commuter corridor, the highest-volume and lowest-risk proof point.

close.title: The South Pacific's most iconic lagoons, re-platformed as a silent waterway.
close.body: The islands are all on the water and minutes apart by sea. A foiling-electric tier glides silently over the reef — the commuter spine, the Leeward crown and the atolls beyond, zero-wake and zero-emission where it matters most.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: French Polynesia, re-platformed as a silent foiling network — commuter spine to Leeward crown to the atolls.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II across the Society/Leeward lagoons (≤70 nm); Quanta-LR hybrid for the cross-archipelago and atoll legs (amber-dashed roadmap)
steady_state.tam_framing: A territory of 118 islands moving high-value tourism and resident traffic by ageing diesel ferry, costly inter-island flight and resort speedboat — a captive premium-transfer pool concentrated on protected water.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a silent foiling network spanning French Polynesia — the Tahiti–Moorea commuter spine, the Leeward resort crown linked island-to-island, and a Quanta-LR reach to the Tuamotu atolls and Marquesas. The most beautiful lagoons on earth, moving without wake or noise.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $75M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 55% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 55% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM — matured network
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market (induced demand); we already capture ~55% — growth is demand + width, not a capture ramp

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — induced marine-transfer market
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food + stays + experiences (≈3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

rungs.label: Partner platform revenue on Navier
rungs.basis: platform commission on journey GMV routed through the Navier network (subset of full Journey GMV)

ceiling_sibling.label: Platform revenue ceiling — 18% × full Journey GMV
ceiling_sibling.derivation: journey_gmv.mid × 0.18 (full GMV ceiling, not Navier-corridor subset)
ceiling_sibling._doc: Sibling reference. Do NOT promote to a 7th ladder rung. Platform_rev rung remains the Navier-subset Interpretation-A value.

phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 122 boats = $41M transport rev = 5,969 t CO2/yr (~$338K rev/boat).

Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: French-Polynesia platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
